| BR13 | A published version of the document is never edited in place: a breaking change is a new major version with a migration note and a new pin | Arch v5 slides 20 and 38; RWB-PLT-NF02-APP |
| BR14 | The delegation table, its versions and its holders stay in rwb-access (P4); the routing rule (lowest covering level, no-holder rule, one-level-up escalation) belongs to rwb-decision (P7) and reads the level, the holder and the substitute on this contract with a 2 s read budget; the approval stores delegation_limit_id, approval_level and limit_version only, with no join, view or foreign key into rwb_access | Ownership Map v1; Arch v5 slides 14 and 41; TSD P4 v3; TSD P7 v2 T3.3; RWB-E2-013 section 11 |
| BR15 | The service holds the delegation version in a local read-through cache, warmed at start before readiness and refreshed on DoaLimitChanged, with the effective date as the switch; no table is copied, and an alert fires when the cached version is older than the version in force | Arch v5 slides 14 and 41 (rwb.access.events.v1); legacy section 3 and section 13 |
| BR16 | The authorise request carries caseId, teamCode, ownerUserRef, escalatedToRole and escalatedAt; it is version v1 with BACKWARD compatibility, so a case service adds an attribute without breaking the access service | Arch v5 slide 14; FSD P4 A2.4 and A2.14; TSD P4 v3 T-A; RWB-E2-015 section 12 |
